digest.component_or_area: comment hygiene detector and CI linter
propositions: 8 of 18 source code comments cite unresolvable commit SHAs due to rebase-on-submit policy, and run/job/thread IDs rot with retention windows; historical narrative belongs in the ticket system, not source code.

A block-level comment/docstring scanner must detect rot-prone patterns (hex SHAs >=7 chars, run/job/thread IDs >=8 digits after keyword, dated incident narratives combining past-tense verbs {failed, broke, regressed, fixed, caught, observed, hit, crashed, flaked} with YYYY-MM-DD or Month DD YYYY dates) and reject blocks that do not cite a ticket/epic/story/bug/ADR ID or carry an 'context: external' escape hatch.

All detector hits at HEAD must be remediated by: (a) citing a resolvable ticket ID in hex-grouped (4x4) or word-triple-alias form, (b) dropping rot-prone tokens and keeping durable current-state prose, or (c) replacing SHA narratives with behavioral descriptions findable via git log.
The word-triple-alias acceptor pattern must reject hyphen-joined path/extension sequences but accept sentence-final aliases to avoid false accepts on file names like sync-hardening-proposal.md.

CI integration as a named step in _build-and-test.yml must block merges on newly introduced rot-prone refs, pass the remediated tree with zero in-tree suppressions, and use EXCLUDED_FILES to self-exclude the guard's own unit-test fixtures.
A policy note must clarify that source code is for current state and concise rationale; historical detail and dated incidents belong in the ticket system.
